do.name: ASTRA open air museum in Dumbrava forest
do.detail: Farmsteads, watermills and wooden churches moved here from all over the country, spread along paths round a lake.

do.name: Climbing the Council Tower over the squares
do.detail: A narrow medieval stair ends on a deck above Piata Mare, looking across the tiled roofs and their eyebrow windows.

do.name: Driving the Transfagarasan to Balea Lake
do.detail: The high road south of the city switchbacks to a glacial lake near two thousand metres, and shuts once the snow arrives.

do.name: The two squares and the Bridge of Lies
do.detail: Piata Mare and Piata Mica sit one behind the other under the Council Tower, joined by the first cast iron bridge in the country. The eyelid dormers in the roofs around them are why the town looks like it is watching you.

do.name: Hiking the Cindrel and Fagaras mountains
do.detail: Marked routes start above Paltinis and Rasinari, with the higher Fagaras ridges an hour further out for longer days.

do.name: Fortified Saxon churches at Biertan and Valea Viilor
do.detail: Villages east of the city keep walled churches built for siege, two of them on the UNESCO list, easy as a day out.

do.name: Sibiu International Theatre Festival
do.detail: For ten days in June the squares, courtyards and theatres fill with performances from companies around the world.

do.name: Floating in the salt lakes of Ocna Sibiului
do.detail: Old salt workings a short drive north hold water dense enough to keep you up, with a small spa resort beside them.

do.name: Brukenthal National Museum
do.detail: A Habsburg governor's palace on the main square holding the oldest public art collection in Romania.
